c.tagline: Morocco's desert film capital and gateway to the Sahara.

taxi.fareNote: Petits taxis are shared beige cabs for short hops around town; there are no ride-hailing apps, so agree the meter or a flat fare before setting off. Grands taxis (older Mercedes) handle longer runs to Ait Benhaddou and the valleys.

emergency.note: 19 reaches the police (Surete Nationale) in towns and 15 is the ambulance/medical service; 177 reaches the Gendarmerie Royale on rural roads outside the city.

avoid.reason: Faux guides and studio-tour touts cluster around Taourirt Kasbah and the film studios; agree taxi and tour prices before setting off.

hood_desc: The walkable downtown along Avenue Mohammed V, packed with cafes, restaurants, shops and tour agencies; the easiest base for first-timers who want everything within reach.
The historic quarter around the earthen Kasbah of Taourirt and the Cinema Museum, opposite the artisan center; best for travelers who want sights and old-Morocco atmosphere on their doorstep.
A quieter district just south of the center with intimate riads and guesthouses, Atlas Mountain views and easy reach of the Atlas Film Studios; suits those wanting calm over bustle.
A residential neighborhood by the hospital and airport on the northwest edge of town; practical and low-key, a handy quiet spot before flying or driving on.
The famous fortified ksar village 30 km west, a UNESCO World Heritage kasbah and film backdrop; an overnight stay lets you photograph it at sunrise before the day crowds arrive.

water.note: Locals drink the chlorinated tap water, but most travelers stick to bottled to avoid stomach upsets.

transit.hours: There is no scheduled service; petits taxis run through the day and grands taxis and coaches leave from the gare routiere, thinning out after dark.
transit.note: Ouarzazate has no city bus, tram or metro network; getting around town relies on shared beige petits taxis, and longer hops use grands taxis and intercity coaches.
transit.pay: Petits taxis are paid in cash (dirhams) to the driver; short in-town rides cost only a few dirhams. There is no transit card.

bus: Supratours coaches to Marrakech, Agadir and the Draa Valley
Grands taxis to Ait Benhaddou, Zagora and Boumalne Dades
train: No rail service; the nearest station is Marrakech, about 4 hours by road over the Tizi n'Tichka pass

transit.m: Petit taxi to the town center (5-10 min)
Many hotels offer free or cheap airport pickup on request

tip.r: ~10% at restaurants; rounding up taxis and cafe bills is appreciated.

landmarks: Aït Benhaddou
A UNESCO-listed fortified mud-brick village stacked dramatically above a desert river, the world's most filmed ksar and an unmissable half-hour trip from Ouarzazate.
Kasbah Taourirt
A labyrinthine 17th-century kasbah of the Glaoui dynasty in the city center, its painted cedar ceilings and crenellated towers ranking among Morocco's finest earthen architecture.
Atlas Film Studios
One of the world's largest film studios, where guided tours wander Egyptian temples, Tibetan monasteries and Roman sets left by Gladiator, Kundun and countless epics.
Musée du Cinéma (Cinema Museum)
Opposite Kasbah Taourirt, this delightfully ramshackle museum lets visitors roam old sets, props and cameras from Ouarzazate's decades as 'Ouallywood.'
Fint Oasis
A ribbon of palms, gardens and Berber hamlets hidden in a rocky canyon just south of town, offering an idyllic taste of oasis life.
Kasbah Tifoultoute
A romantic crumbling Glaoui kasbah perched above the Ouarzazate River, where storks nest on the towers and the terrace serves sunset mint tea.
Kasbah Amridil (Skoura)
A superbly preserved 17th-century kasbah in the Skoura palm grove, once pictured on Morocco's 50-dirham note, an easy day trip along the Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs.
Noor Ouarzazate Solar Complex
One of the planet's largest solar power stations, its luminous tower and sea of mirrors shimmering on the desert horizon like a science-fiction mirage.
El Mansour Eddahbi Reservoir
A vast turquoise lake amid lunar desert hills east of town, popular for birdwatching, boat trips and serene sunset views over the water.
Place Al Mouahidine
Ouarzazate's palm-shaded central square, flanked by craft shops and cafés, the relaxed gateway for browsing carpets and Saharan souvenirs before desert departures.

train.note: There is no railway south of the High Atlas - ONCF's network (https://www.oncf-voyages.ma/) ends at Marrakech, about four hours away over the Tizi n'Tichka pass. Arrive by coach or grand taxi, or fly into Ouarzazate's small airport.

bus.note: No international coaches. CTM (https://www.ctm.ma/) and Supratours (https://www.supratours.ma/) run from the bus station to Marrakech in about 4 hours on the spectacular but winding Tizi n'Tichka road, and east through the Dades and Todra gorges to Erfoud and Merzouga for the dunes. Book CTM online; shared grand taxis cover the shorter hops to Ait Ben Haddou and Skoura.

ferry.note: Ouarzazate sits on the edge of the Sahara with no navigable water, so there are no ferries. The Mansour Eddahbi reservoir nearby is a water supply, not a transport route.

half.name: Dades Gorge
half.blurb: A river canyon lined with red rock formations and Berber villages lies about ninety minutes northeast of Ouarzazate.

half.name: Todra Gorge
half.blurb: A narrow limestone canyon with sheer three-hundred-meter cliff walls sits roughly two hours from Ouarzazate.

full.name: Zagora
full.blurb: A Draa Valley palm oasis town and gateway to the Sahara dunes lies about two and a half hours south.
